sessionTitle: Scale agentic AI cost‑efficiently on Azure with Arm Cobalt VMs

announcements.name: Azure Cobalt 200 VMs in preview
announcements.shortDescription: Announced by Satya Nadella in the morning keynote, the Cobalt 200 processor is custom-built by Microsoft for server workloads and natively supports Azure Boost
announcements.longDescription: Satya Nadella announced the Cobalt 200 VMs in the morning keynote, building on the Cobalt 100 launched in 2024. Like Cobalt 100, the Cobalt 200 is an in-house, custom-built processor purpose-built by Microsoft for server workloads and optimized for Microsoft's first-party workloads as well as a variety of third-party workloads. Cobalt 200 VMs come innately supported with Azure Boost.

announcements.name: At least 50% better per-core performance over Cobalt 100
announcements.shortDescription: Cobalt 200 is built on 3nm technology on the latest Arm architecture and delivers roughly 50% better per-core VM performance than the prior generation
announcements.longDescription: The Cobalt 200 processor is built on 3nm (three nanometer) technology on the latest Arm architecture. Its per-core VM performance is at least 50% better than the previous generation. Industry benchmarks (such as SPECrate) and Microsoft benchmarks were tested on the VMs and compared against the previous generation on a per-vCPU performance basis.

announcements.name: Expanded VM family
announcements.shortDescription: Beyond the D, DP, and ECDS series carried over from Cobalt 100, new memory-optimized VMs offer about 16 GB of memory per core, plus dense local-storage-optimized LCDS VMs aimed at agentic AI and cloud-native workloads
announcements.longDescription: Beyond the D, DP, and ECDS series carried over from Cobalt 100, Cobalt 200 extends the lineup with a memory-optimized version in which every core gets about 16 gigabytes of memory. It also adds dense local-storage-optimized LCDS VMs aimed at agentic AI and cloud-native workloads. Together these VM offerings are intended to fit any enterprise or cloud-native workload.

announcements.name: Preview region availability
announcements.shortDescription: Cobalt 200 is currently previewed in eight regions, with expansion planned at general availability
announcements.longDescription: Cobalt 200 is currently in preview in eight regions, with plans to expand to more regions at general availability (GA). The speaker highlighted that Cobalt 200 is well suited to agentic AI and cloud-native scenarios such as sandbox creation, request loops, and fitting many sandbox agents into a single VM. The session then transitioned to a demo presented by Pranay.

announcements.name: Live on-cluster agentic inference demo
announcements.shortDescription: A polyglot microservices shopping-cart application runs across mixed Cobalt 100 and Cobalt 200 nodes, with CPU-based LLM inference and a shopping agent executing entirely inside the AKS cluster
announcements.longDescription: The demo shows a cloud-native polyglot microservices shopping-cart application running across a cluster with mixed Cobalt 100 and Cobalt 200 nodes, with microservices on Cobalt 100 and the orchestration on the more capable Cobalt 200. The Cobalt 200 nodes perform CPU-based LLM inference without needing any external accelerators, with everything running locally inside the AKS [inferred] cluster so data never leaves and no third-party LLM is called. An orchestrated family of agents manages the inferencing entirely on CPU within the trusted, local cluster.
